=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (multiple leaflets are attached along the rachis at different levels, indicating an alternate arrangement along the stem structure)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (the leaflets are densely packed along the rachis with very little space between them)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3.	Leaf complexity (simple / compound): compound (the leaf is composed of multiple distinct leaflets attached to a central axis)
    4.	Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): odd-pinnate (the leaflets are arranged along a central rachis, and a single terminal leaflet is present at the apex of the leaf structure)
    5.	Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): >10 (there are clearly more than 10 leaflets visible on each side of the rachis, appearing to number 20 or more per leaf)
    6.	Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): alternate (the leaflets are arranged alternately along the rachis, not in direct pairs)
C. Leaf Morphology
    7.	Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (the margins of the leaflets appear smooth and continuous without teeth or serrations)
    8.	Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (the overall leaf structure is long and narrow, tapering towards the apex and base)
    9.	Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (the tip of the leaf is pointed)
    10.	Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (the base of the leaf tapers to a wedge shape where it attaches to the stem)
    11.	Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (veins branch off from a central midrib in a feather-like pattern)
    12.	Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): clearly visible, closely spaced, numerous (fine veins branch off the midrib at regular, close intervals)
    13.	Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (the leaf surface reflects light, indicating a smooth, glossy texture)
    14.	Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no hair-like structures are visible on the leaf surface)
    15.	Petiole length (short / long): long (the petiole extends significantly from the base of the leaf structure, though the full length is partially obscured)
    16.	Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (the petiole appears round in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17.	Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (the stem appears thin, green, and flexible, lacking the thickness and bark of a woody stem)
    18.	Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no hairs are visible on the stem)
    19.	Stem color: green (the visible portion of the stem is green)
    20.	Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (the stem surface appears uniform without ridges or lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21.	Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are visible at the base of the petiole)
    22.	Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex is visible)
    23.	Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no pulvinus is visible at the base of the leaf or leaflets)
    24.	Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils are visible)
F. Notes: The seedling is resting on a decaying log. A pink tag with "ENTESC 3" is attached to the leaf. The leaflets are small and numerous, giving the leaf a fern-like appearance.
